To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

VEGF-A expression, VEGFR-1 expression, and the VEGF-A: VEGFR-2 ratio were associated with poor prognosis and that the VEGF-B: VEGFR2, VEFG-C: VEGFR1 and VEGF-C: VEGF3 ratios were associated with the presence of lymphocytic infiltration in mismatch repair-proficiency colorectal cancers.
the VEGF-A to VEGFR ratio was associated with the presence of perinodal inflammation, lymph node metastasis and poor survival.
the VEGF-A to VEGFR2 ligand/receptor ratio may be a useful prognostic tool in mismatch repair-proficiency colorectal cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ligand/receptors ratios in the progression of colorectal cancer.
the role of the ligand/receptors ratios of the VEGFR pathway in the progression of colorectal cancer.
the evaluation of the role of VEGF family members on the progression of mismatch proficient colorectal cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evaluation of the VEGFR1/2 ligand/receptor ratio may provide a more detailed understanding of the involvement and potential prognostic value of these proteins in mismatch repair-proficiency colorectal cancers.
VEGF ligands, receptors and ligand to receptor ratios play a significant role in the biology of mismatch repair proficient colorectal cancer.
VEGF ligands and receptors have important roles in the development of colorectal tumours and that the VEGF-A to receptor ratio is of potential clinical value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VEGF-A:VEGFR1 ligand/receptor ratio is a potential biomarker for the presence of lymphocytic inflammation in the tumour stroma.
a higher VEGF-A to VEGFR2 ligand to receptor expression ratio may identify patients with a more aggressive tumour behaviour.

the ratio of VEGFA to VEGFR2 is an independent prognostic marker for survival in patients with colorectal cancer, and that the ratio of this marker to the receptor VEGFR1 may be an independent prognosticator for survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evaluation of the VEGFR1/VEGF-A ratio may be a useful prognostic tool for predicting the outcome of mismatch repair-proficiency colorectal cancers.
the evaluation of the VEGFR/VEGF ratio is a more accurate way of determining VEGF involvement in tumour progression.
VEGF-A expression, VEGFR expression and the ratio between VEGF-A to VEGFR may be important in the development and progression of colorectal cancer.
